Show less Read more Like 175 Dislike Reply 16 replies Hide replies 16 replies @basilthecat9 1 month ago my main take away is that I would now like to see Elordi as a henchman Show less Read more Like 33 Dislike Reply @spaceodds1985 1 month ago (edited) Elordi IMO is too young, and with an Oscar nod to his name his price and marquee standing has shot up. Turner is IMO the perfect choice; perfect age, perfect standing career wise and if the rumours of Steven Knight’s script characterising Bond as even more of a blunt instrument then ever before, is true, then Turner gives off the mannerisms and personality of such a character. Hope he gets the role. Show less Read more Like 76 Dislike ❤ by @calvindyson Reply 1 reply Hide replies 1 reply @legorickdeckard229 1 month ago I vote Turner, I like that he seems unasuming yet a bit menacing. I can totally see him utter a sardonic quip after dispatching someone. Show less Read more Like 58 Dislike Reply @ryanfrasor9403 1 month ago It’s Turner hands down for me. I really get the Fleming vibe from him, fits the Carmichael description more than any other actor being discussed. He still the show in Masters of the Air. Show less Read more Like 34 Dislike Reply @TheBookish1 1 month ago Turner for me. Out of the two of them, he’s the one who I can see having served in the military/navy. Without sounding odd, he has that same killer look as Craig does. I think given what Steven Knight has said, they’re stripping this franchise back, and I think Turner would work perfectly with that. Show less Read more Like 74 Dislike Reply 5 replies Hide replies 5 replies @RickAstley2308 1 month ago Plot twist: it's Patrick Gibson Show less Read more Like 65 Dislike Reply 4 replies Hide replies 4 replies @arthurbonisseurdelabath7925 1 month ago Callum "it's just a jump to the left" Turner Show less Read more Like 24 Dislike Reply @jacksonwayneputnam1599 1 month ago I had never really heard of Turner until the Bond casting rumors. My first thought when seeing him is how much he resembled literary Bond. And after seeing more of his performances and public appearances, I do think he can capture the presence needed for the role. I like Elordi, but I’d almost rather see him as a Bond villain. He’d be great as the ‘dark parallel’- much like Robert Shaw, Sean Bean, Toby Stephens. I mean, even if he ended being a re-interpretation of Jaws.. I’m kinda all for it. Who knows what kind of artistic interpretation Denis Villeneuve could bring to that. He handled scenery chewing weirdo villains in ‘Dune’ very well; he could do something interesting with a literal scenery-chewer. Show less Read more Like 30 Dislike Reply 1 reply Hide replies 1 reply @thebutterstick8659 1 month ago Not sure if either will be picked but my vote between the two goes for Turner. Elordi just doesn’t seem to fit for me. Plus he’s becoming a little too mainstream for the whole “up and coming” vibe. Plus he’s crazy tall. I think it makes him a deliberate candidate, after all, we know that Villeneuve has a BIG respect for the original works that his adaptations are based on. Fleming would be proud...
